title: AI is quietly becoming an unofficial and potentially unwanted 'third' in relationships
excerpt: People are increasingly turning to AI to talk about their relationships, but relying on chatbots can weaken empathy and communication skills.
content_html:
Lindsey Hall, a writer based in Texas, suspected the man she was seeing was using AI. Uncertain about where things were going, she asked him outright what made him want to be with her.

"You're fun, smart, pretty," she summed up his response. "The way it was written was so cold and so formal and so ChatGPT. I just remember being so turned off by that."

One night, about five months into dating, she happened upon a conversation he'd had with ChatGPT in which he expressed serious doubts about their relationship. "I'm just not proud of her," she said he'd written. He apologized after being confronted, and they dated for a few more months before breaking up.

"I felt like I was in a relationship with me, him, and the robot," she said.

AI is taking on a new role in human relationships. A Pew Research Center survey published last month found that one in five adults aged 18 to 29 said they used AI chatbots for emotional support or advice. A new YouGov survey found that 13% of US adults, and 23% of those under 30, said they had shared a secret or problem with a chatbot that they hadn't told a human.

Chatbots can help people reflect, organize their thoughts, and prepare for difficult conversations, but experts in psychology, relationships, and AI told Business Insider that problems can arise when people start relying on AI instead of talking to their partners. Chatbots are also prone to excessive validation, which can make it harder for the person using them to empathize with their partner or see the other side of a situation.

Rachel Wood, a cyberpsychology researcher and founder of the AI Mental Health Collective, said while the impact of AI on jobs and the workplace is evident and widely discussed, she thinks the impact on human relationships could be even greater, and could take years to play out.

"AI is shifting the relational bedrock of society," she said.

Turning to chatbots for emotional support

Confiding in a chatbot about your relationship can feel easier than talking to another person because there's no social risk, according to Ashleigh Golden, a licensed clinical psychologist who works on AI and mental health. It can also be validating, she said. Whereas a partner or friend might push back and encourage you to consider your own behavior, chatbots might not.

A study published in Science in March compared responses from 11 leading large language models with responses from humans and found the AI systems were nearly 50% more sycophantic, including when users described unethical, illegal, or harmful behavior. The authors found that a single interaction with a sycophantic AI made the study participants less willing to take responsibility or make amends with someone, and also increased their conviction of being right.

"You get the safety of disclosing to a stranger plus the felt sense of being deeply understood without any of the risk of being seen," Golden said.

Engaging with a chatbot also does not require many of the skills essential to maintaining human relationships, Wood said, such as patience, listening, negotiation, empathy, and compromise.

"Those muscles will atrophy," she said, "which will in turn make us worse at our relationships because we're not practicing listening and holding space for each other."

Sharing with a chatbot instead of your partner might also feel like a betrayal to them, said Idit Sharoni, a licensed marriage and family therapist specializing in couples therapy and affair recovery. She said if you're confiding in AI about your relationship, your partner may feel like the chatbot has more access to your inner world than they do.

"It totally can feel like emotional infidelity," she said.

A recent survey of 3,500 US users of the dating app Hily found that 70% of Gen Z respondents and 60% of millennials wouldn't date someone who relies on AI to make sense of their feelings. More than half said they would be uncomfortable with a partner discussing their shared sex life with AI.

When using a chatbot can help

Keven Cotton, a controller at the Shakespeare Theatre Company in Washington, DC, said communication has not always been his strong suit during his six-year marriage, but that talking with AI has helped. After one disagreement with his wife, he said ChatGPT helped him consider how they may have misread each other and think through how to reopen the conversation.

He thinks talking about his relationship with AI has worked for him because therapy gave him a solid foundation for examining his own behavior rather than looking for validation.

"You have to do the work to maximize what you're getting out of AI," he said. "If you're coming at it from a victim standpoint, it's going to give you victim responses."

Sharoni said chatbots could be useful when someone already knows what they want to discuss but needs help finding a way to bring it up. Issues can arise, she said, when using AI to interpret how the other person feels or make a judgement call based on one-sided facts.

If AI does help you work through your feelings, Wood recommends sharing that with your partner so it's not happening in secret. She suggested saying something like, "Hey, this is what the chatbot is reflecting back to me. What do you think about that?"

Couples may also want to establish their own rules for using AI, Golden said, including whether it's acceptable to vent about the relationship and whether concerns processed with a chatbot should eventually be brought back to the other person.

She said AI can be useful as a "pre-processing space," helping someone turn an initial messy feeling into something they can bring back to their partner, but that the risk is when AI stops being used as a "bridge" and becomes a "destination."

A chatbot can help you reflect or prepare, Cotton said, but it can't actually do the work of participating in a relationship.

"AI can't show up for you," he said.

content_html_zh:
德克萨斯州作家林赛·霍尔 (Lindsey Hall) 怀疑她所见的男人正在使用人工智能。 由于不确定事情的进展，她直截了当地问他是什么让他想和她在一起。

“你很有趣、聪明、漂亮，”她总结了他的回答。 “它的写作方式是如此冷酷、如此正式，如此 ChatGPT。 我只记得我对此非常反感。”

约会大约五个月后的一天晚上，她偶然发现了他与 ChatGPT 的一次谈话，其中他对他们的关系表示了严重怀疑。 “我只是不为她感到骄傲，”她说他写道。 他在被质问后道歉，他们又约会了几个月才分手。

“我觉得我与我、他和机器人建立了一种关系，”她说。

人工智能正在人际关系中扮演新的角色。 皮尤研究中心上个月发布的一项调查发现，五分之一的 18 至 29 岁成年人表示，他们使用人工智能聊天机器人来寻求情感支持或建议。 YouGov 的一项新调查发现，13% 的美国成年人和 23% 30 岁以下的人表示，他们曾与聊天机器人分享过未告诉人类的秘密或问题。

聊天机器人可以帮助人们反思、组织思想，并为困难的对话做好准备，但心理学、人际关系和人工智能专家告诉《商业内幕》，当人们开始依赖人工智能而不是与伴侣交谈时，就会出现问题。 聊天机器人还容易受到过度验证，这会让使用它们的人更难同情他们的伴侣或看到情况的另一面。

网络心理学研究员、AI Mental Health Collective 创始人 Rachel Wood 表示，虽然人工智能对工作和工作场所的影响显而易见并被广泛讨论，但她认为对人际关系的影响可能更大，而且可能需要数年时间才能显现出来。

“人工智能正在改变社会的关系基石，”她说。

转向聊天机器人寻求情感支持

研究人工智能和心理健康的持证临床心理学家阿什利·戈尔登 (Ashleigh Golden) 表示，向聊天机器人倾诉你们的关系比与另一个人交谈更容易，因为没有社会风险。 她说，这也可以得到验证。 虽然伴侣或朋友可能会反对并鼓励您考虑自己的行为，但聊天机器人可能不会。

3 月份《科学》杂志上发表的一项研究将 11 种主要大型语言模型的反应与人类的反应进行了比较，发现人工智能系统的阿谀奉承程度要高出近 50%，包括当用户描述不道德、非法或有害行为时。 作者发现，与阿谀奉承的人工智能的单次互动使研究参与者不太愿意承担责任或与某人和解，同时也增加了他们对自己正确的信念。

戈登说：“你可以安全地向陌生人透露信息，而且可以感受到被深入了解的感觉，而不必担心被看到的风险。”

伍德说，与聊天机器人互动也不需要维持人际关系所必需的许多技能，例如耐心、倾听、谈判、同理心和妥协。

“这些肌肉会萎缩，”她说，“这反过来会让我们的人际关系变得更糟，因为我们没有练习倾听和为彼此保持空间。”

专门从事夫妻治疗和婚外情恢复的持证婚姻和家庭治疗师伊迪特·莎罗尼（Idit Sharoni）表示，与聊天机器人而不是你的伴侣分享信息也可能会让他们感觉像是背叛。 她说，如果你向人工智能吐露你们的关系，你的伴侣可能会觉得聊天机器人比他们更能接触到你的内心世界。

“这完全感觉像是情感上的不忠，”她说。

最近对约会应用程序 Hily 的 3,500 名美国用户进行的一项调查发现，70% 的 Z 世代受访者和 60% 的千禧一代不会与依赖人工智能来理解他们感受的人约会。 超过一半的人表示，他们会对伴侣与人工智能讨论他们共同的性生活感到不舒服。

使用聊天机器人可以提供帮助

华盛顿特区莎士比亚剧院公司的控制员凯文·科顿 (Keven Cotton) 表示，在他六年的婚姻中，沟通并不总是他的强项，但与人工智能交谈有所帮助。 在与妻子发生一次分歧后，他说 ChatGPT 帮助他思考他们可能如何误读对方，并思考如何重新开始对话。

他认为谈论他与人工智能的关系对他来说很有效，因为治疗为他检查自己的行为而不是寻找验证奠定了坚实的基础。

“你必须努力最大限度地从人工智能中获得收益，”他说。 “如果你从受害者的角度来看待这个问题，它会给你受害者的反应。”

莎罗尼说，当有人已经知道他们想讨论什么但需要帮助找到提出的方法时，聊天机器人可能会很有用。 她说，当使用人工智能来解释他人的感受或根据片面事实做出判断时，可能会出现问题。

如果人工智能确实可以帮助你处理你的感受，伍德建议与你的伴侣分享，这样它就不会秘密发生。 她建议这样说：“嘿，这就是聊天机器人向我反映的内容。 你对此有何看法？”

戈尔登说，夫妻可能还想制定自己的人工智能使用规则，包括是否可以接受发泄感情，以及通过聊天机器人处理的问题最终是否应该返回给对方。

她表示，人工智能可以作为“预处理空间”发挥作用，帮助人们将最初的混乱感觉转变为可以带给伴侣的东西，但风险在于人工智能不再被用作“桥梁”而成为“目的地”。

科顿说，聊天机器人可以帮助你反思或准备，但它实际上无法完成参与关系的工作。

“人工智能无法为你显现，”他说。
